content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a configuration with [article_no] modules all linked via Ethernet. When I toggle an input from one [product_name], it triggers an output on another [product_name]. During simulation, everything works smoothly, but in actual hardware, I sometimes observe delays of up to 10 seconds before the output responds. Could this be due to using too many network inputs? I've attached my test application for reference. Has anyone else experienced similar delays, or perhaps had a similar setup that worked without any issues? I've tried many solutions, but I'm currently out of ideas and really want to resolve this delay. Thanks, [user_name]

Thread closed because the question was posted twice. The second discussion with the topic about delay when pressing a button is published within the [product_name] conference. Best regards, [user_name] (Moderator)

analysis.insight_summary: A user is experiencing notable delays (up to 10 seconds) when outputs are triggered between multiple [product_name] modules over Ethernet in a real setup, although simulations show immediate responses. The contrast suggests possible network performance problems, especially regarding the scalability and reliability of distributed systems with several modules. The feedback points toward latency concerns related to networked input/output operations in such environments.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks prompt or near-instant responses between modules over Ethernet, comparable to simulation performance. Seamless and dependable triggering across the network is expected, even with a high number of networked inputs.
